sentences.text: Angela Rayner has defended her decision to pause plans to redraw local council boundaries, saying she wanted to ensure they would survive legal challenge.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The local government secretary also told the BBC she wanted to be "clear-eyed" about what the planned shake-up in 16 areas of England was likely to achieve.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: It comes after earlier this week she abandoned proposals in four other areas, in the face of legal threats from Reform and Conservative-led authorities.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The surprise announcement on Monday has thrown the reorganisation plans into doubt, and drawn criticism from local leaders preparing for the changes.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Councils in affected areas have been drawing up proposals and consulting with residents since the reorganisation was announced in late 2024, in a process that is already thought to have cost millions of pounds.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC's Political Thinking with Nick Robinson podcast, Rayner conceded the decision to press pause had been "difficult" and she understood local authorities had put a "lot of time and effort" into their plans.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: But she added she wanted to have "all the information" about the proposals before going ahead with them, after her reappointment to her cabinet role under Andy Burnham, ten months after her resignation last year .
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: "I got the legal advice and I hadn't had the time to review and to go through all of that, and court cases were looming," she told the podcast.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: "If I'm making a decision that is highly likely to be in legal challenge, I want to make sure I've dotted my i's and crossed my t's," she added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Rayner also said she wanted was "really clear-eyed on where we were going" with the plans, after Burnham had asked her to look again at the blueprints, which were announced by her predecessor Steve Reed.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson Plans for major overhaul of councils halted Council to take government to court over reforms In her announcement on Monday, Rayner said she was withdrawing plans to reorganise councils in Essex, Hampshire, Norfolk and Suffolk.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Those proposals, announced in March, were already subject to legal challenges from Reform-led councils in Essex, Norfolk and Suffolk, and the Conservative-led administration in Hampshire, which were lodged over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: She also said she wanted to review plans for 16 other areas, including 14 announced by Reed days before Burnham replaced Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister and reappointed her to her old role.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Some councils affected by those plans, including Kent and Leicestershire, had threatened similar bids to challenge the lawfulness of the decision-making process.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The government has argued that the plans, which will abolish remaining two-tier areas in England where county and district councils share responsibility for services, would make local government more effective and cost efficient.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: However, critics said the plans would not save money, while diverting resources from front-line services and leaving councils more remote from their communities.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Others have also complained that the reorganisation could stymie or delay parallel efforts to merge councils into regional authorities led by mayors, which Burnham has cited as a key part of his economic plans.

sentences.text: Molly and Taylor met in their 20s and how they organise money as a couple has changed over time When Molly and Taylor Haylett started their family, they hadn't really planned for what it would mean financially.

sentences.article_title: I asked my husband to pay into my pension when we had a child - here's why

sentences.text: At the start of summer, in the pillared room in 10 Downing Street, Andy Burnham looked out at his new special advisers, the few dozen political officials tasked with driving hundreds of thousands of civil servants to deliver his government's agenda.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Some had been with him in Manchester or Makerfield.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Others had spent the past few months trying everything to prevent his hostile takeover of Sir Keir Starmer's government - and the new prime minister showed he was aware of it, going out of his way to praise those who had stayed on, for their efforts in the preceding years.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: At that meeting, Burnham's team mapped out four key moments in the coming months.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: First, the return to Parliament in September, when Burnham and other leading ministers would make their first statements to MPs.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Second, Labour's annual conference at the end of September - Burnham's first as leader.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Third, the Budget, taking place on 28 October.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: And fourth, the 10-year plan for Britain which Burnham intends to unveil in November.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: As MPs prepare to leave Parliament on Tuesday for almost a month and party conference season gets underway, the first phase of that route map is almost complete - enough for figures at all levels of the Labour Party to begin answering some questions about the shape of this new government.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Most importantly, perhaps, how new actually is it?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Does Burnham represent continuity or change?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: That question is especially relevant because those Labour MPs who pushed for Sir Keir to be replaced always fell into two broad camps: those who wanted a change of style and emphasis but continuity in policy, and those who wanted a major shift in policy.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Both groups saw what they wanted in Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Andy Burnham speaks during his first Cabinet meeting since becoming prime minister Going by the words of the new prime minister himself, he represents a profound break with the past, and not only the immediate past.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: In his first speech as Labour leader in July, Burnham described his ascendancy as "the most significant change moment in our politics for 40 years".
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: That is the timeframe he has returned to again and again, signalling not just a desire to reverse issues he believes stem from the Thatcher era but also to break with aspects of the Labour governments since then, including his immediate predecessor's.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Some in government are already quietly questioning, though, whether the ambition of that rhetoric can be squared with the early signals emerging from the Treasury under the new Chancellor John Healey.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Who's in Andy Burnham's cabinet?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: In interviews over recent weeks, and especially in his first major speech on Monday , Healey has said he will stick to Rachel Reeves's commitments not to increase the main rates of income tax, national insurance and VAT, as well as her rules on government borrowing.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: In the speech, he promised to "control public spending", and hailed Reeves for beginning to "recover Britain's fiscal discipline".
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: It led to opposition parties labelling Healey a continuity chancellor.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: A similar critique is being voiced among some of his government colleagues.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Most are more generous for now, arguing that Healey's first imperative - especially at a time of turmoil in the global bond markets - is reassurance, and that the Budget is the moment for him to show how he plans to substantiate Burnham's rhetoric.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: And finding ways to boost regional growth has been one of Healey's major causes since he was a junior minister at the Treasury more than 20 years ago - long before it was at the heart of Burnham's political personality.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: There is no question, though, that this week the minister who most starkly signalled change from the previous government was a man who coveted Healey's job - Ed Miliband, who was instead appointed foreign secretary.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: The sanctions announcement was received with near-universal warmth from Labour MPs, itself a marker of change from the Starmer government.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: It was also seen as a sign of the ability of Miliband in particular, but this government in general, to drive its agenda through the civil service machine.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: "There is a much clearer sense now from No 10 of what they want," one official who worked under Sir Keir as well as Burnham says.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: "Before there was a bit too much of 'let us know your ideas for what we should do', now it's 'this is what the PM wants, give us options to deliver it'." That is a culture shift which Burnham sought to drill into his cabinet at their weekly meeting on Tuesday, still only their third such meeting.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: According to one present, the prime minister said: "We need to be on the front foot.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Let's get on and do things.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: The new attorney general, Ellie Reeves, has pared back rules introduced under Sir Keir which some ministers believed forced them to be over-cautious about legal risk, thereby slowing down or blocking new policies altogether.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Louise Haigh , Burnham's deputy, has vowed to "strip out needless bureaucracy" from government more generally, citing an example of there being three public consultations between 2019 and 2023 on whether to microchip cats.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: "If we can't microchip cats without getting tied up in red tape, it should come as no surprise the public is losing faith that governments can get things done," she said.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: As Burnham moves into the next phase of his autumn, there is a recognition from some around him that he will need to produce some more significant policies to underpin his rhetoric.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Those in government familiar with early work on fleshing out his commitment to "public control" of essential services insist the direction of travel is truly radical.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Haigh is responsible for this, chairing a taskforce on how to reverse "over-privatisation" specifically of housing, water, energy and transport.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Burnham may offer more details on these policies at Labour's conference, while he is likely to wait until after then to show his hand on whether he wants continuity or change when it comes to Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's reforms to the legal immigration system - a much more divisive issue among Labour MPs.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: And whatever their differences on policy, Labour MPs are united on one thing.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: The fundamental reason they installed a new prime minister was because many of them believed that continuing on the same path meant losing the next general election.

sentences.text: For them, a long-term improvement in Labour's poll ratings would be the most important change of them all.

sentences.text: The 1998 fantasy romcom, starring Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman as witchy sisters Sally and Gillian Owens, received mixed reviews from critics when it was first released.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: But it's put a spell on a new generation discovering it online, with some now regarding the film as a cult classic and autumn staple.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: The demand for a follow-up by this new wave of fans helped convince Bullock and Kidman to reprise their roles nearly 30 years on, they say.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: "You never get the opportunity to do something where people really are asking you, 'please do it'," says Bullock.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: "It's usually us going to them." Actresses Joey King and Maisie Williams are joining the cast this time round to play Sally's daughters, Kylie and Antonia.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: Kissing Booth star King tells BBC Newsbeat she feels this desire for nostalgic content, which has become one of the defining forces within entertainment in recent years, has been influenced by "the world moving so fast".
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: Practical Magic 2 sees the cast return to a world which is steeped in powerful ancestral magic "I think with technology moving at the speed that it is, we're really missing the times when we were less reachable," she says.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: "If we couldn't figure out something, we'd stare out the window until it came to us, and I think we're nostalgic for a time like that." She feels this can also be a strength of cinema as it can help "make memories" and "feelings" for people that they can revisit by rewatching.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: The upcoming release comes at a time when reboots, reunions and remakes are dominating film and TV lists.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: Game of Thrones star Williams agrees the drive for nostalgic content feels like a "symptom of people longing for simpler times", but says she is "very grateful" that they have made a sequel and not a remake.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: "I do believe in pushing the story forwards and I do believe in telling new stories," she says.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: "And I do believe stories can come back around and they can still be meaningful.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: There are also nods to the original throughout, with bubbling family tension, dark romantic "witchcore" fashion and the iconic midnight margaritas.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: US acting stalwarts Dianne Wiest and Stockard Channing return to their roles for the follow-up, while Guardians of the Galaxy actor Lee Pace, Cobra Kai's Xolo Maridueña and House of the Dragon's Solly McLeod are new additions.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: Reviews so far have been mixed, with the Guardian describing it as a "nostalgia-bait return" , external which is as "strange and messy as the first" but with "warm seasonal pleasures to be had".
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: Meanwhile The Hollywood Reporter , external says the "slapdash" sequel "works better the less you look for any sense of logic, and the more you just lean into the transient joys of watching these actresses bounce off each other".
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: Joey King says the idea of "being witchy" can be "empowering right now" Amid the scrutiny around the film, Williams admits joining the Practical Magic world was "a little bit overwhelming", but says the cast were "so supportive the whole time" and "welcomed us into the sisterhood".
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: The bond of sisterhood is at the heart of the first film and continues in the sequel, but Bullock has recalled this was initially one of the criticisms of the original , external , with some branding it as "too witchy" with "too many women".
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: With women's rights under pressure in some countries, Williams says it is a "challenging time" and she feels it's "so important in a time like this for women to be supporting one another".
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: "We are in a time when young women are staying in education longer and women, before having children, are sometimes being paid more than their male counterparts, which I do find to be really exciting," she adds.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: "But there's a lot of work to do.
sentences.article_title: People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars

sentences.text: "And this feeling of witches, symbiosis and power - I feel like there's something in that which can just push us forwards." Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here .

sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the impact on partners - and what you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Prof Ama Johal, a consultant orthodontist and sleep expert at Aerox Health, explains that the partner of a snorer can become "so impacted upon that it's almost a last-ditch effort on their part to get up and go sleep in a separate room because they have to sleep".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: He adds: "As humans we physically can't function without that necessity." Prof Ama Johal says many couples put up with the negative effects snoring for too long During the night, we cycle through different stages of sleep in repeating patterns, usually every 90 minutes.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: The deeper stages of this cycle are important for physical restoration.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If sleep is frequently disrupted, you may spend less time in the restorative stages, meaning you can wake up feeling tired, even if you've spent a lot of time in bed, the BSSAA explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Your brain processes and stores information from the day during sleep.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Fragmented sleep - which can happen if you're waking up due to a snoring partner - can interrupt this process, impacting your focus and memory.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Disrupted sleep can also impact hormone regulation, which affects your energy levels and motivation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sleep also plays a role in regulating the brain systems involved in stress and emotional response.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: When it is disrupted, these systems can become less balanced, which may make you feel more irritable and less able to cope with stress.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: This is something Meg Warren, 29, experienced when her former partner's snoring would keep her up.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says: "Without fail, after a snoring-induced wake up I would feel on incredibly high alert." Meg, a charity media officer, would prod him throughout the night and try to coax him from his back to his side.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says she would wake up "feeling groggy and dazed, sometimes so much so that it would feel like a hangover".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Meg Warren felt 'groggy and dazed' after a night of little sleep due to her former partner's snoring Anna-Louise Dearden, a 52-year-old journalist, says she sometimes sleeps in a separate room from her partner due to his snoring.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Having this option allows her to prioritise getting enough rest when the snoring is particularly bad.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: There are things that can be done, say both Simon and Johal.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But first, it is important to distinguish whether your partner is simply snoring, or whether they have sleep apnoea.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "What you don't want to do is simply make someone quieter at night while potentially missing an underlying sleep-related breathing disorder," Simon says.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Signs of sleep apnoea, a disorder that causes a person's breathing to repeatedly stop and start during sleep, include pauses in breathing, choking at night, waking frequently, and suffering from morning headaches.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If this is what you are dealing with, you could be recommended a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machine, or even surgical treatment in some cases, Simon explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: For simple snoring, Simon said that lifestyle changes can make a difference, such as losing weight, stopping smoking, reducing alcohol intake before bed, or changing your sleeping position - such as laying on your side rather than your back.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: You can also suggest to your partner that they see a GP, who will be able to advise further or refer you to a specialist.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: An expert might suggest treating nasal obstruction or allergies, if this is what is causing snoring, or wearing a custom mouthguard to gently push the lower jaw forward and keep the airway open.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Johal says too many couples put up with snoring "for too long", which impacts their relationships and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "The key thing is that there is help out there, it's just tapping into it." How sleep tracking can make your sleep worse The hidden cost of the night shift and how to sleep it off
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Spanish intelligence services warned of social media calls for a mass migrant crossing into Ceuta the day before tens of thousands of people entered the territory, newly released government documents show.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: The revelations emerged in documents declassified by the Spanish government amid accusations it failed to give the full story of the migrant influx.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: On 29 July, Spain's National Intelligence Service (CNI) told Moroccan and Ceuta authorities that social media groups were encouraging migrants to cross the following day.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has insisted that the events of 30 July were impossible to predict, but opposition parties say the documents show the government misled Spaniards.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: Sánchez had previously told parliament that there was "no information that conveyed the magnitude" of the "crisis we were going to suffer" on the last two days of July.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: At least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: Most swam around a border fence and at least 100 people died during the crossing, according to figures from Ceuta's mayor.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: Although most returned, as many as 5,000 remain in makeshift camps or are sleeping on the city's streets and beaches, leading to unrest in the autonomous Spanish city in North Africa.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: Locals have expressed safety concerns and some have destroyed shelters and blocked aid being supplied to the migrants .
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: In a note on 29 July, the CNI told Moroccan intelligence it had identified WhatsApp and Facebook groups promoting an attempt by migrants to reach the Spanish exclave the following day, "both swimming and via the [border] fence".
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: The messages are part of a tranche of more than 40 security documents linked to the Ceuta crossing that the government declassified following mounting pressure on Sánchez over his handling of the crisis and widespread allegations in Spain that Morocco had played a role in facilitating the crossings.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: Earlier this month, a leaked Spanish police report seemed to implicate Moroccan police in the incident.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: However, Sánchez has maintained that there is no evidence suggesting Moroccan complicity.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: But opposition politicians said the newly released material contradict that claim.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: "They had the information, they are directly responsible for the invasion of Ceuta and for those who died," said Ester Muñoz of the conservative People's Party.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: Jorge Buxadé, of the far-right Vox, said on social media that the documents showed that Sánchez "and his band of criminals should be brought before the Supreme Court for treason and security crimes".
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: The government has continued to insist that it acted according to the information available.
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares said he was "not aware of any report that might have foreseen the magnitude of what happened on July 30".
sentences.article_title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge

sentences.text: A government source said the published documents "showed that the information available before the mass crossing did not make it possible to anticipate the scale that the crisis would reach or prepare with enough time the necessary response".

sentences.text: But unlike an ordinary convention, no official party business was conducted in Dallas, with the event instead serving as a rally for Republicans who are seeking to boost turnout and avoid losing control of Congress in November.

sentences.text: President Donald Trump, whose grip over the party remains absolute, delivered a lengthy keynote speech on Wednesday during the opening night of the two-day event.

sentences.text: He covered many of the subjects he has returned to time and again this year - with a few surprises thrown in.
sentences.article_title: Four key takeaways from  Republican midterms convention

sentences.text: Here are the key takeaways from his address.
sentences.article_title: Four key takeaways from  Republican midterms convention

sentences.text: The vast arena was filled with diehard Trump supporters sporting red MAGA gear from his past presidential campaigns.
sentences.article_title: Four key takeaways from  Republican midterms convention

sentences.text: A decade after his first White House run, Trump is still beloved among his base and he has bent the party to his will in the years since.
sentences.article_title: Four key takeaways from  Republican midterms convention

sentences.text: The old-style Republican establishment, or what's left of it in the Trump era, was nowhere to be seen.
sentences.article_title: Four key takeaways from  Republican midterms convention

sentences.text: Senator Susan Collins of Maine and other Republicans running in competitive races chose to stay away.
sentences.article_title: Four key takeaways from  Republican midterms convention

sentences.text: The absence of more moderate Republicans was glaring and offered a reminder of just how much the party has changed.
sentences.article_title: Four key takeaways from  Republican midterms convention

sentences.text: It also raised questions about the effectiveness of holding an unprecedented midterm convention in the first place.
sentences.article_title: Four key takeaways from  Republican midterms convention

sentences.text: The core audience, both in the arena and watching on television, appeared to be Trump loyalists, not the moderates and swing voters the Republican Party needs to turn out in large numbers in November.

sentences.text: York, pictured, is one of the cities where the regional mayor plans to limit the new levy to 5% of an overnight stay Labour's regional mayors in England have pledged to cap a new fee on visitors' overnight stays at 5%, after hospitality bosses warned it could put jobs at risk.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Local leaders are set to gain new powers to charge an uncapped levy, dubbed a "tourist tax", as a percentage of the cost of hotels, bed and breakfasts and other types of accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: But the Labour mayors in 10 city regions said they would voluntarily limit the charge if they do apply it, adding that they had listened to concerns over costs.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Reform UK's two regional mayors and the two Conservative ones are likely to oppose any levy given criticism from their national parties of the policy.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: In a letter to Chancellor John Healey and Local Government Secretary Angela Rayner, the Labour metro mayors said 5% represented a "reasonable ceiling" on the tax.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: "It provides a balance of ensuring that local levies are not excessive, or vary significantly between regions, while also leaving room for local variation as appropriate," they added.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: They added this would still allow for "meaningful investment" in local areas, whilst stressing any future levies in their areas would be "subject to local consultation".
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: The letter was signed by Labour mayors in London, Greater Manchester, Liverpool City Region, West Midlands, North East, West of England, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, East Midlands and York and North Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: The government had earlier pledged to protect budget holidays "by making sure low-cost accommodation always pays lowest levy" and said the extra cash could be invested in high streets and local transport.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: While Labour mayors have backed the new levy, others have expressed caution or signalled they will not bring it in.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Local leaders, including heads of Foundation Strategic Authorities where there is no mayor, will need to clarify by early 2028 how the revenue raised should be reinvested.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: They will also be allowed to offer exemptions, such as for campsites.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: However, mayors will not be allowed to exempt whole localities within their regions from the tax, to avoid creating confusion for visitors and businesses.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: The government said it would introduce a bill to Parliament "in due course" to bring in the levy, which would apply to both Britons and people visiting from abroad.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Leading trade body UKHospitality has hit back, saying the levy means "jobs are now at risk".
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: "We know, don't we, that local government is struggling for funds - it was hit very hard by austerity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: A 5% tourist tax for overnight stays was introduced in Edinburgh in July The idea was first raised under former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer in November and is similar to schemes running in Scotland and European destinations.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Two cities in England already run their own voluntary schemes - a £1 per room, per night City Visitor Charge in Manchester, introduced when Burnham was mayor of the region, and a £2 nightly charge in Liverpool.

sentences.text: These are business-led schemes where hotels choose to pool the money raised to support local tourism.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Nant Ffrancon is one of the most special and unique landscapes in Wales but experts say its habitats have deteriorated Some of Wales' most endangered species are "at risk of vanishing" from an area of the country's largest national park, experts have warned.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: The National Trust said Nant Ffrancon, a valley in Eryri National Park, was facing "serious ecological decline" with some species in danger of disappearing altogether, including the mountain blackbird and the mountain finch.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: Now, a new £1m scheme is aiming to restore and conserve more than 4,000 acres of habitats at Eryri, also known as Snowdonia .
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: "We're in a very serious situation - we're in a nature emergency.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: There are so many species in this valley which are on the brink of extinction," said Simon Rogers from the National Trust.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: From the high peaks of Cwm Idwal to the deep valleys of Dyffryn Ogwen, Nant Ffrancon is one of the most special and unique landscapes in Wales.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: But experts say its habitat has deteriorated and some of Wales' most threatened species, including the ring ouzel bird, are in danger of disappearing altogether.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: Now, a project led by the National Trust will work together with local communities, tenant farmers and volunteers to restore and protect 4,040 acres of habitats.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: Rogers said there was a "unique variety of habitats" in the area and warned many species "really are on the brink".
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: The ring ouzel bird has been in decline across the area "One of the ones we've chosen to look at particularly in this project is the ring ouzel - a bird that's red-listed," he explained.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: "It's been in decline massively in the area and across the whole country, and this is one of the last strongholds for it.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: "So we'll be looking at that little bird, understanding how they use the landscape here and doing our best to manage the land to ensure their survival for the future.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: "There are a lot arctic alpine flowers that grow in Cwm Idwal as well, one of them being the Tufted Saxifrage, where there were only seven individuals at the start of the year - all of them growing here in Cwm Idwal.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: "But with the drought we've had this year, only three have made it through the summer.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: Ecological surveys and regular monitoring will map the impact of the restoration work, using species such as the woodcock and otter, and plants including aspen and juniper to give an idea of the health of the valley.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: The work will also build on innovative use of GPS livestock collars to manage grazing more precisely.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: Cwm Idwal Partnership Officer Rhys Wheldon-Roberts said monitoring was "really important because it allows us to graze in the right areas at the right densities and at the right time".
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: He added: "The collars on the cattle allow us to move the cattle around the landscape and you can monitor it as you go, and the farmers can see that data live on their apps.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: "It can make grazing something much more effective for the cattle and for nature." As well as local farmers, there will be an emphasis on community involvement and volunteering as part of the work.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: "There are opportunities for people to get involved in monitoring, in volunteering, just learning about the landscape in general," said Wheldon-Roberts.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: "Here in Cwm Idwal we have lots of school visits every year and they'll be able to see the effects of the project and the effect that the cattle are having in that conservation grazing way, so it's really exciting in that regard as well.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: "What we're trying to do with this project is set a foundation for the future," said Rogers.
sentences.article_title: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park

sentences.text: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has told police chiefs that lessons must be learned from how they handled last weekend's anti-migrant protests in Dover and Portsmouth - saying she expects officers to use all powers necessary.

sentences.text: Anthony Lee and his wife Laura pleaded guilty at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday The Conservatives' former director of campaigning and his wife have pleaded guilty to cheating at gambling by placing bets on the date of the 2024 general election.

sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: On Thursday at Southwark Crown Court, Anthony Lee pleaded guilty to two offences and Laura Lee pleaded guilty to one offence.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: They will be sentenced in October.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: This video can not be played Prince William wants 'environment where people can speak openly' before reaching crisis The Princess of Wales has made a surprise appearance alongside her husband the Prince of Wales, as he gave an impassioned call to the sports sector to help prevent suicides.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: "Sport can help save lives," Prince William told sports players, mental health charities and sports industry figures at Everton's football ground in Liverpool.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: He was launching a project that wants to use sport to help open conversations and end the stigma surrounding mental health.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: "Sport has the ability to reach people who may never walk through the door of a mental healthcare service," he said.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: Everton's football ground hosted Prince William's suicide prevention project The On Your Side project wants to give people confidence to start the "difficult conversations" with friends, relations, teammates or colleagues who might be struggling with their mental health and might be at risk of suicide.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: It is being supported by sport stars including England football captain Harry Kane, retired British middle distance athlete Dame Kelly Holmes, and former England football star Alan Shearer.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: Royal sources said that Catherine wanted to attend to "highlight the difference that can be made when people feel able to talk openly about how they are feeling and when someone is there to listen".
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: "Never underestimate the difference that you can make," said Prince William, stressing that suicide prevention was "not someone else's responsibility".
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: "It belongs to all of us," he said.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: Talking of hidden anxieties, he added: "We do not always see what is happening behind closed doors, or understand the battles that may be taking place beneath the surface." Dame Kelly talked of her own struggles: "We talk about suicide, which is the end for that journey.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: What we forget is that journey has happened for a long period of time.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: What we need to avoid is that journey coming to that endpoint." Dame Kelly Holmes talked about the mental health challenges facing sports players It was important that sports stars admitted their own vulnerability, said Olympic cyclist Dame Laura Kenny.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: She spoke movingly of how a family member had tried to take their life and how she felt "almost ashamed to admit that this could happen in my family because it's not a subject that is easily spoken about".
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: The cyclist also described the darkness of her feelings after the loss of two babies, through a miscarriage and an ectopic pregnancy, "which ultimately ended up in an emergency situation".
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: On Your Side aims to use the reach of sport to raise awareness about suicide and to show people the help available in a crisis, with the Football Association, Premier League and Team GB providing support.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: The level of suicide is disproportionately higher among men than women - it is the biggest cause of death for men under the age of 50 in the UK - and sport is seen as an effective way of communicating that help is available.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: "My hope is that every sporting organisation in the country will look at what is being launched today and ask a question: 'What more can we do?' Because the opportunity before us is enormous," Prince William said.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: The royal couple saw a bench at the ground dedicated in memory of Gary Speed , a footballer who once played at the club, and who died by suicide in 2011.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: The bench, unveiled last year, is intended to give people a space to speak openly about their anxieties and the royal couple met Speed's mother there.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: Shearer was a friend of Speed and is backing the call for people to try to support people they have worries about.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: "You don't have to be an expert.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: You don't have to have all the answers," said Shearer.
sentences.article_title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide

sentences.text: Kane delivers the message: "If you think someone's not ok, ask." Prince William helps to narrate the video, which wants to open up conversations about mental health, with 7,000 lives being lost to suicide each year in the UK.

sentences.text: Malcolm Potier is the former laird of the Hebridean island of Gigha A 75-year-old man who strangled a woman after she started to sing along at a West End show has been jailed for two years.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: Malcolm Potier was sitting near victim Kirsty O'Donnell in the audience at We Will Rock You at the London Coliseum in June 2023.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: He said he had no recollection of being at the show, or of attacking O'Donnell, but was sentenced at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday after being found guilty of non-fatal strangulation by jurors.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: Potier, a businessman and surveyor of Sarratt near Watford, was already jailed in Australia two decades ago having twice tried to arrange the murder of a former partner following a dispute over their child.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: He is also the former laird - a Scottish term for someone owning a large long-established estate - of the Hebridean island of Gigha.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: Judge Dafna Spiro said his behaviour was "extreme and horrific".
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: "It is an unusual offence," she said.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: "It's not a situation I have ever come across before." She said there was a "thread" of "dominance, control and lack of accountability" in Potier's behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: O'Donnell was sitting in the dress circle at the London Coliseum when she was attacked Prosecutor Sam Lubner said Potier had been at the show, which is based on the music of the rock band Queen, with his theatre critic partner Lizzie Loveridge.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: He said O'Donnell and a friend had started singing, then Loveridge - using a profanity - told them to "shut up".
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: O'Donnell suggested the reaction was "rude", but Potier responded by saying "I'll show you what rude is" before attacking her.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: The court was told the attack lasted a few seconds.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: Potier and Loveridge were later tracked down thanks to the business card she had given out to O'Donnell, and he was arrested in November 2023.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: O'Donnell was not physically injured, but she told the judge she was "more wary" of her surroundings since the attack and "far more conscious" of her "physical safety".
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: "I want to set an example for the young women and girls in my life, that this sort of behaviour is not acceptable," she said.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: She also described hearing Potier "laughing" outside court during the trial, talking about his belief that he would not be given a prison sentence partly because of his age.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: The judge was told how Potier was given a six-year jail sentence in 2002 for inciting the murder of his former partner in Australia.
sentences.article_title: Theatregoer who throttled woman at show is jailed

sentences.text: He was given a further 12-year sentence in 2006 for trying to arrange her murder again.

sentences.text: Two people have been arrested in London on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service, the Metropolitan Police has said.

sentences.article_title: Two arrested in London on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service

sentences.text: The suspects, who were both held on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service, have been released on bail under strict conditions until late October, the Met said.
sentences.article_title: Two arrested in London on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service

sentences.text: Police said the arrests were not "connected to any of the incidents or attacks" linked to Jewish and Iranian communities across London earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Two arrested in London on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service

sentences.text: The arrests took place following two searches carried out at properties in north and north-west London in June, the Met added.
sentences.article_title: Two arrested in London on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service

sentences.text: Commander Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said she knows "news of these arrests will come as a concern to some members of the public" but stressed she does "not believe there to be any imminent threat to the wider public".
sentences.article_title: Two arrested in London on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service

sentences.article_title: Two arrested in London on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service

sentences.text: "As we've shown here, if we suspect any activity could threaten the safety of the UK or the public, then we will not hesitate to take action." She added the UK's terror threat level was severe and called for people to be vigilant.

sentences.text: The new battery-electric TransPennine Express trains are set to enter service in 2034 Work to create the UK's first battery-electric trains for long-distance main line services is set to begin in 2028, the Department for Transport (DfT) has announced.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The 29 new Adessia Stream trains are expected to enter service in 2034 and will be built at Alstom's Litchurch Lane factory in Derby.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The government said the investment of almost £1bn would help support more than 350 jobs at Alstom and a further 6,000 jobs across the UK supply chain.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the new trains would deliver "faster, more reliable journeys to the north and thousands of British jobs for the next generation".
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The managing director UK at Alstom said the fleet would "transform" journeys across northern England He added: "I've lost count of the number of times someone has stopped me to tell me about the train that never came.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: "And when that happens, it means missed shifts, missed appointments, and missed opportunities.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Today, that starts to change." The DfT said the trains would help deliver the Transpennine Route Upgrade's aim to boost capacity by 30%, with thousands of additional seats a day across the Pennines by the early to mid-2030s.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: They will run between key destinations across the north including Liverpool Lime Street and Scarborough, Manchester Airport and Saltburn, and Manchester Piccadilly and Hull.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The DfT added that journey times will be cut by up to 10 minutes between Manchester and Leeds and up to 14 minutes between Manchester and York.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The trains will be bought by Rock Rail and leased to TransPennine Express, the government added.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Alstom, which boasts the largest rolling stock train manufacturing site outside of China, secured a £370m contract in 2024 to produce 10 new London Elizabeth line trains.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: This came less than three months after a redundancy consultation put 1,300 jobs at risk at its Litchurch Lane factory, which dates back to 1876.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Rob Whyte, managing director UK at Alstom, called the latest agreement a "landmark moment for Britain's railway".
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: He said: "We couldn't be prouder that the country's first main line battery-electric trains will be designed and built in Britain.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Step-free boarding - the "elimination of gaps between the train and platform" - are also being promised as part of a commitment to accessibility, alongside three dedicated wheelchair spaces, two accessible toilets, family-friendly areas and cycle and buggy storage on each train.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: A coroner has ordered 24,000 pages of documents be handed over for the inquest into the death of Sara Sharif A coroner leading the inquest into the death of Sara Sharif has ordered Surrey County Council to disclose more than 24,000 pages of documents.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: Sara, 10, was found dead at her family home in Woking, with her father Urfan Sharif and stepmother Beinash Batool jailed for life in 2024 for murder.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: A pre-inquest review heard that the inquest, originally scheduled for April, will be pushed back by a further six months to October 2027.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: The eight-week inquest will examine what state agencies knew, or ought to have known, about Sara's safety before she was murdered.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: At the hearing in Woking on Thursday, senior coroner Richard Travers told the county council that he wants "all of the pages" to be disclosed to him by 2 October.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: He said he would call the local authority's chief executive Terence Herbert to appear before the court if he did not have them.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: Alethea Redfern, representing the authority, argued against the full disclosure of the documents, saying that many were "irrelevant" to the inquest.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: But Travers said he does not understand what the council's "issue" was with him obtaining the files.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: When she died, Sara had 71 injuries including broken bones He said: "This is going to be an order of the court.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: It is not up to Surrey County Council to decide what's to be disclosed and what's not to be disclosed." Three individuals due to give evidence at the inquest also applied for anonymity in press reporting.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: Travers said he would make a decision on that application at a later date.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: In July, lawyers for Batool asked for the inquest to be held in front of a jury, who it was argued would have a "helpful perspective".
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: Sara Sharif was violently abused in a "campaign of torture" lasting two years.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: A review into her death found that services in Surrey failed to properly investigate why Sara started wearing a hijab - that covered her bruising - for "fear of causing offence".
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: Concerns were also raised about Sara's care within a week of her birth in 2013, and her parents were known to social services as early as 2010, it has been reported.

sentences.text: Surrey County Council has previously apologised for what happened and said it had taken "robust action" to address earlier findings.
sentences.article_title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files

sentences.text: People will be able to go to their local chemist in England this autumn and get on-the-spot treatment for 12 common conditions without going to their GP first.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Pharmacists can already prescribe medication for seven conditions -  sore throat, earache, sinusitis, shingles, impetigo, infected bites and urinary tract infections.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Five more - migraines, acne, scabies, ear infections and badly blocked noses - are now also being added to that list.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: NHS England said the move was to ease pressure on busy GPs and A&E departments while making sure people could get treatment quickly and conveniently.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: After a very hot summer and three of the busiest months on record in A&Es in England, the NHS says it wants to make it as easy as possible for people to get help when they need it for everyday conditions.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said people were "fed up with the scramble for routine appointments" and wanted help close to home, with no more taking time off work or waiting to get seen.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: "For five more common conditions, you'll be able to walk into your local pharmacy and get treated on the spot," he said.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Mr Burnham said families would feel the change, and the plan would give people back "precious time".
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: There will be a gradual rollout and the service will eventually be available at thousands of community NHS pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Community pharmacies also offer support with healthy eating, exercise, stopping smoking, monitoring your blood pressure, contraception, flu and Covid vaccinations.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: The charity the Migraine Trust said it was delighted by the news after calling for more help for migraine care in pharmacies.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Chief executive Rob Music said having this support for people with migraine through their local pharmacy was "a wonderful opportunity for a faster and improved care pathway".
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Dr Amanda Doyle, director for primary care and community services at NHS England, said she wanted to make sure that patients can get as much support as possible in their communities, "so they do not have to be admitted to hospital unnecessarily".
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: But bodies representing pharmacies across England have consistently said that the funding provided by the goverment does not cover the workload for the new plans.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: "Pharmacies are still under significant financial pressures," said Henry Gregg, chief executive of the National Pharmacy Association.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: "This shows why the government should go much further and invest in our pharmacy network that has the power to transform people's experience of everyday health issues." The Pharmacy First scheme started in England in 2024.

sentences.text: August was the joint-hottest month ever recorded, tying with July 2023, according to the EU's climate service.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: The record was driven by a combination of climate change and the rising influence of El Niño, pushing heat into the atmosphere across the Pacific.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: Temperatures for the month were 1.65C above pre-industrial levels - surpassing the critical 1.5C threshold agreed by countries to avoid the worst consequences of climate change.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: While a single month above 1.5C does not mean it has been permanently crossed, it shows a trend towards breaching that limit.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: The month also capped western Europe's warmest summer, with high temperatures pushing the season past the deadly heat of 2003.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: Dr Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at Copernicus, described August as "a remarkable month in the global climate record", and its impacts had been "increasingly being felt by communities, economies and ecosystems across the world".
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: The combination of record air temperatures, record ocean heat and Europe's exceptional summer showed how climate change was now driving extremes across "both the atmosphere and the oceans", she said.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: World's oceans hit highest temperature on record UN climate chief Simon Stiell said the record clearly showed humanity's impact on the climate.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: "The evidence is irrefutable: this is the spiralling price of humanity's fossil fuel addiction, and the global climate crisis it is fuelling," he said.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: On top of the ongoing impact of the use of fossil fuels, the rise of a powerful El Niño is making matters worse, the researchers have said.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: El Niño is a natural climate pattern in which a band of the eastern Pacific turns unusually warm, releasing vast amounts of stored ocean heat into the atmosphere and nudging global temperatures upwards for around a year.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: The one currently being experienced is still strengthening and could become one of the most powerful on record, according to the Copernicus team.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: The biggest impact of this natural phenomenon on global temperatures is expected to hit over the coming year, meaning the current run of records may have further to go.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: The impact of El Niño is expected to impact monsoon rains and storms in Asia such as here in the Philippines, where tens of thousands of people were recently displaced by floods That prospect follows a summer that drove western Europe to its warmest on record.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: This was echoed in the UK, which had its hottest summer since records began in 1884 - a high mark the Met Office found had been made around 130 times more likely by human-caused climate change.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: This figures carried "a very real human cost", said Dr Clair Barnes, an extreme weather researcher at Imperial College London.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: The heat across the UK and Europe disrupted schools, strained hospitals, hit food production, fuelled fires and drought, and claiming "tens of thousands of lives", she said.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: She rejected the idea that such summers were now simply the "new normal".
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: "Until we stop burning fossil fuels these records will continue to tumble, and the extremes will worsen faster than we are able to adapt.
sentences.article_title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat

sentences.text: Crucially, how much worse we allow it to get remains within our hands." Additional reporting Erwan Rivault What questions or concerns do you have about El Niño?
