sentences.text: Jayden Long, 19, and Eddie Hill, 20, were walking on a mountain range in Eryri Two friends who died on a mountain ridge during extreme winter conditions tried calling 999 but the alert was not escalated "as it should have been", according to a police expert at an inquest.

sentences.text: The bodies of Eddie Hill, 20, and Jayden Long, 19, both from Dereham, Norfolk, were found by a mountain rescue team in Eryri, also known as Snowdonia , on 19 February.

sentences.text: Chinese firms dominate battery production Europe has taken some big swings in the battery industry in recent years and has made a couple of high-profile misses.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Both Sweden's Northvolt , external and Norway's Morrow , external filed for bankruptcy and there are fears in Europe that the continent has missed another technology shift.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: With more transport and industry switching from fossil fuels to electricity, batteries are likely to be a growth business.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: But the length of time required to bring new products to market, coupled with brutal competition, especially from China, means taking a substantial risk.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Could the answer lie at an almost unimaginably small scale?
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: An increasing number of investors and researchers think so.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: A single nanometre is one-billionth of a metre, but it's at that level that some of the most consequential work is being done.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "If you can make this work, it touches so many industries [but] it's a risky business," says Christian Rood, chief executive of Dutch tech firm LeydenJar.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Named after a 18th century precursor to electric cells, LeydenJar uses a technique known as plasma deposition to make a lighter, more efficient anode – an essential component of all batteries.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Silicon is a highly effective and cheap material to use in anodes, but pure silicon expands and contracts as the battery operates and is recharged, which causes it to crack.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: However, using plasma deposition, LeydenJar can - layer by tiny layer - make an ultra-thin pure silicon foil which resists cracking, allowing a significant increase in battery life, charging speed, and energy density (up to 50%, according to LeydenJar).
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "Where normally a pure silicon anode would fall apart, [this] remains stable, so it was a very wonderful invention," says Rood.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "We address the bottleneck in the battery." LeydenJar's tech could mean better batteries Commercial-scale production will start at the end of 2026, but it has taken 10 years to get to this point – the very definition of the time and investment required for so-called Deep Tech innovations.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: It's no coincidence that LeydenJar's factory is in the Dutch city of Eindhoven - home to ASML and other important players in the computer chip industry.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "A lot of people talk theoretically about ecosystems; I can tell you this is one of our sources of competitive advantage," Rood says.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "It's really the crossover from semiconductors to batteries that makes us different - once you've demonstrated the principle in the lab, industrialization requires you to work with the semiconductor technology and suppliers.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "That means a lot of risk, but also a lot of opportunity in terms of patenting, in terms of securing your whole intellectual property.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: And that's much more difficult to do in the US or in China." Across the Netherlands and Europe more widely there are multiple smaller Deep Tech start-ups looking to develop nanotechnology in the battery market.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: One of those is Powall, a start-up in the Dutch city of Delft that is developing commercial-scale equipment for nanocoating the powders that are the raw materials of today's batteries.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Again, the scale is tiny, and once again the technique was born in the semiconductor industry.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Individual powder granules are measured in micrometres, the coatings in nanometres - they are applied using a technique known as atomic layer deposition.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Roderik Colen, CEO of Powall, tells me that the system offers multiple opportunities to adjust and improve the performance of today's batteries.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.

sentences.text: Most common by far is injecting the gel-like substance hyaluronic acid - the same key ingredient used in lip fillers.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Hyaluronic acid is a naturally occurring sugar molecule in the body and is known as a "moisture magnet" as it grabs hold of water.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Dr Javed Hussain performs a range of cosmetic procedures, including penis fillers Dr Javed Hussain has been offering penis fillers for more than a year at his clinic in Prestwich, Greater Manchester.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Hussain trained as a doctor before moving into cosmetic procedures, but penis fillers do not legally require any medical training to perform.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He says demand is increasing.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He's treated men of all ages - some in their mid-20s, while his oldest client is aged 72.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: The process starts with consultations on the patient's health, reasons for wanting to have the procedure, expectations about the results, and a discussion about the risks.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: On the day of the event itself, a penis is injected with hyaluronic acid three times - on the top and on either side.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: The hyaluronic acid filler is delivered through a cannula that enters at the base and travels along the length of the shaft.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: The equipment needed, including cannulas and syringe, to perform a penis filler procedure The filler is then massaged to give an even look, which the patient continues at home.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: At a cost of up to £3,500, Hussain says men can expect between 10% and 20% more girth for the next six to nine months.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: These range from relatively minor ones such as soreness, bruising and uneven filler, to serious ones including infection.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: These risks apply to all procedures using filler.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: However, there is also a risk of damaging the vital structures and blood vessels in the penis that are needed for an erection.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: When asked why he feels comfortable offering procedures that are concerning surgeons, Hussain says he "totally understands" why some are worried.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "It comes from the right place, that nervousness," he says, "but at the same time, more and more evidence is growing and we're getting the results" and that "there is a benefit" to men.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Hussain says he has an "immediate action plan" including drugs to quickly dissolve the filler in the event that things go wrong, and reports that "thankfully, we've never needed to" - although the BBC cannot independently corroborate that.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: But he recalls one patient who came to him for advice after treatment elsewhere, which had "really gone wrong".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He says the incorrect type of filler had been used and the "shaft of the penis was starting to become black" as the procedure had damaged the blood vessels in the penis and the skin was dying.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: The man was sent straight to A&E.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Prof Vaibhav Modgil has seen men for whom penis enhancement procedures have gone wrong Prof Vaibhav Modgil, an andrologist and consultant urological surgeon for the NHS in Manchester, has seen these men coming into hospital after botched procedures.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "When it does happen, it can be devastating for the patient," he says.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He recalls seeing men with "skin necrosis, where an area of the skin dies off it turns very black and then it sort of sloughs off.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "So, men will go in thinking, 'Oh, it's gonna be brilliant', but they might come out actually being even more dissatisfied than when they went in." Alex, who did not want his real name to be used, travelled to Germany for a different type of penis enhancement procedure.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He had surgery to cut the ligament that attaches the penis to the pubic bone to make it appear longer.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He also had his own fat cells harvested and injected into his penis to enlarge it.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: When he woke up after the procedure, he was in so much pain he couldn't stand.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "I sustained a lot of bruising and all my upper legs turned yellow," Alex says.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "I couldn't walk properly for about a month." Alex was treated in Modgil's clinic where eventually he was given the all-clear.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "Many people do not get that luxury," he says.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "I got off lucky." Alex says he knows he was "never small in the first place", but society and porn had convinced him that a bigger penis was "masculine and the best".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: There is a lack of data on how fillers affect the penis long-term Despite a lack of official data on the number of penile enhancement procedures, Modgil says online search trends, advertising and social media all "points to the fact that the numbers are on the up".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: This has led the British Association of Urological Surgeons to issue new recommendations against these procedures.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "The guidance that we've recently produced essentially says we cannot recommend that any of these procedures should take place because the evidence is so poor," says Modgil.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: It looked at 36 studies, involving 3,750 men, but said it was still not clear what the "safety profile" of these procedures were.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: This is partly down to a lack of data on how fillers affect the penis long-term.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: But there is also concern that - just like lip fillers - you do not need any qualifications to perform the procedure.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Modgil says an outright ban is "probably too severe", but if these procedures are going to continue then the industry "massively needs regulation".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He called for a national registry to record when penis filler procedures have been performed and for long-term data to be collected so men can make an informed decision based on the risks and the benefits.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Back in Manchester, Jason is happy with the results of his procedure and thinks he'll do it again when his current fillers wear off.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Experts recommend that those who may be more vulnerable - such as older people and babies and young children - should take extra precautions.

sentences.text: As the body gets hotter, blood vessels open up.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This lowers your blood pressure and makes your heart work harder to push the blood around the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This process can cause mild symptoms such as an itchy heat rash or swollen feet.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: At the same time, sweating leads to the loss of fluids and salt and, crucially, the balance between them in the body changes.

sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: But as the weather gets hotter, it is harder for the body to keep its core temperature down.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: It opens more blood vessels near the skin to lose heat to our surroundings and starts sweating.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Some exposure to UV is essential for our wellbeing, but too much is damaging and can cause skin cancer.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: UV radiation is emitted by the Sun and penetrates the Earth's atmosphere.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: It enables our skin to produce essential vitamin D, which is important for the function of bones, blood cells and our immune system.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: But too much UV can be harmful.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: It can lead to skin cancer by damaging DNA in skin cells.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: UV also plays a substantial role in skin ageing, contributing to wrinkles and loosened folds.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: A caesarean, or C-section, is a major operation to deliver a baby through a cut in the abdomen, usually just below the bikini line.

sentences.text: Carys Louise Brandon, from Swansea, had an emergency C-section to deliver her first child in 2022 and said she was completely unprepared for what came afterwards.

sentences.text: The Welsh government said every woman should receive high-quality postnatal care tailored to her needs.

sentences.text: Carys' first baby was born in 2022.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: After needing an emergency C-section, Carys, a content creator, said she had many unanswered questions about her recovery.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: The Welsh government has committed to a three-year programme of improvements, but the Royal College of Midwives (RCM) said maternity services had not kept pace with the changing picture.

sentences.text: New mums 'left to get on with it' after C-sections Julie Richards, director of the RCM in Wales, said postnatal care for C-sections should include support with pain relief, wound care and surgical recovery, alongside help with feeding and caring for a new baby.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: She said the rise in caesareans had changed the demands being placed on services.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Ceri Ann had an emergency C-section and her daughter, Ania, was taken to neonatal intensive care because she was not breathing.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Ceri Ann said she was then left alone on the recovery ward, unable to move.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "I just wanted to see my baby but I couldn't, and the staff told me there was no-one available to take me up to see her." She said it was seven hours until she held her baby for the first time, and that was when her husband arrived back at the hospital and took her to the unit himself.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "It was awful, I just cried and cried," she said.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: It acknowledged that being separated from a baby following birth could be distressing and said its teams worked to facilitate contact "at the earliest safe opportunity".
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Nicola Rous-Morgan is a pregnancy and postnatal yoga teacher, and a trained midwife who works with women recovering after childbirth Nicola Rous-Morgan is a pregnancy and postnatal yoga teacher and a trained midwife, who works with women recovering after childbirth, including those who have had C-sections.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: She said women often tell her they feel left alone to manage their recovery by themselves.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "I think one of the biggest take-homes is they felt that once they had been discharged from hospital, upon coming home, that they were just left to get on with it." She added: "The focus is on women who are recovering from vaginal delivery.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: It's not geared towards women who are recovering from major abdominal surgery." Nicola said women should not have to rely on private services or social media to find basic recovery information.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: "These things shouldn't be things that women have to pay for privately.

sentences.text: Richards said: "Our midwives are stretched, and quite often that is often impacted into the postnatal care, into the community settings." The RCM surveyed its members in Wales in July, and 94% of respondents said they were not able to give the care they would like to give.

sentences.text: The organisation said midwives were working extra shifts and being moved to cover shortages elsewhere in maternity services.

sentences.text: Richards said more investment and a workforce plan was needed.
sentences.article_title: New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high

sentences.text: Lucy Shepherd was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2019 A breast cancer survivor says she no longer lives "with the same fear" after a clinical trial enabled her to stop the heart medication she needed following cancer treatment.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Lucy Shepherd, from Hertfordshire, was diagnosed with triple positive breast cancer shortly after her 33rd birthday, but a routine scan revealed that her heart function had declined during care.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: A new study, described as "hugely encouraging" for patients, has found the majority of breast cancer survivors whose treatment caused heart problems may not need to be on precautionary medication for life.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "Being part of the trial and having the chance to come off my heart medication has definitely improved my life," Shepherd said.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: The trial - funded by the British Heart Foundation - involved 90 women in their 40s and 50s across four UK hospitals, whose hearts had recovered after a specific type of treatment for breast cancer.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Most would have been advised to stay on heart drugs for life over concerns heart function would decline if they stopped.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Researchers found that 98% of patients in the group who stopped taking medication had no change in heart function after one year, with just one woman developing a problem with her heart's pumping ability.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Women who came off drugs also reported, in questionnaires, a better quality of life.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Shepherd developed heart problems related to her cancer treatment Shepherd, now 39, said: "Living beyond my cancer treatment was difficult because no one could tell me whether I should stop or continue taking my heart medication.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "As I got fitter after my cancer treatment ended doctors gradually reduced my heart medication dosages, but I was still having side effects like a low heart rate and fatigue.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: I also had the mental burden of remembering to take them and the worry of what would happen if I missed a dose.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "I'm still taking hormone therapy, but I don't live with the same fear I once had.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "Modern breast cancer treatment is a remarkable success story," she said.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "But the damaging effects of these drugs on the heart leaves survivors and their doctors with difficult questions about ongoing treatment to maintain their heart health.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "Our study provides the first evidence that heart failure therapies can be safely stopped in survivors whose hearts have recovered, with the support of ongoing close monitoring.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: But the researchers suggest their findings can start important conversations between survivors and their doctors about whether they need to continue treatment long-term.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Breast cancer is the most common cancer in the UK, with nearly 60,000 new cases diagnosed each year, according to Cancer UK.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Approximately 15 to 20% of breast cancer cases are HER2-positive, meaning the breast cancer cells have higher than normal levels of a protein called HER2 on their surface.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: In about 10% of cases, this treatment causes problems with heart function.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Survivors are currently advised to stay on these drugs for life, even after their cancer treatment ends and their heart recovers.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Dr Sonya Babu-Narayan, clinical director at the British Heart Foundation and consultant cardiologist, said: "These findings will be hugely encouraging for the thousands of breast cancer survivors whose heart health has been affected by lifesaving cancer treatment.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "The study results give hope that many women will be able to safely stop medicines once their heart has recovered." Do you have a story suggestion for Beds, Herts or Bucks?
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: The Lib Dems say schools are approaching an "existential crisis" in teacher retention Burnt out teachers urgently need better working hours and more support to stop them leaving the profession, the Liberal Democrats say, as the new term approaches.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Nearly half of the teachers surveyed by the party in England said they were planning to quit the classroom in the next five years, with many saying they felt overworked and stressed.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Lib Dems are urging new Education Secretary Lucy Powell to fully fund teachers' pay, rather than raiding school budgets to cover increases, and to bring in limits on overtime.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Department for Education said last year saw the lowest rate of teachers leaving the profession since 2010 but acknowledged there was "more to do".
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The survey asked more than 900 teachers, headteachers and Special Educational Needs Coordinators (SENCOs) across England how long they planned to stay in teaching.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Almost half of those in post said they were considering leaving teaching in the next five years, while one in ten were planning to spend less than a year in the job.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: More than three quarters of those surveyed, which included former teachers, said they had felt "frequently or constantly burnt out" while at work.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Respondents cited high workloads on marking, lesson preparation and other tasks, which they said gave them less time in the classroom.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrats' schools spokesperson Caroline Voaden said this pointed to a government that is "not listening" to the profession.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "We rely on teachers to educate our children, the least we can do is make sure they want to come back after the summer," she said.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Teacher retention is a challenge successive governments have had to grapple with.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The National Education Union (NEU) reported that 4 in 10 teachers were planning to quit over "huge workloads and excessive accountability" in 2019.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: This latest survey was also conducted with the help of the NEU, as well as the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL).
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "After over a decade of austerity and chronic underfunding in our schools the system is on its knees" said the NEU's general secretary Daniel Kebede.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "The new academic year is the perfect time for Andy Burnham to signal a fresh start for our schools" he added.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Lib Dem proposals include the government fully funding teacher's pay, which will increase in England by 3.5% from September, with an additional 3% the year after.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Currently, half of the pay increase will come from existing school budgets.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The party is also calling for proper enforcement of teacher's legally mandated working hours, the introduction of reasonable limits on overtime, and for all schools to be required to introduce flexible working policies.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The party did not identify where funding might come from to pay for the policies.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: An education department spokesperson said: "We know teachers do an incredible job and we're determined to make sure that dedication is matched with the right support.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "Last year saw one of the lowest rates of teachers leaving the profession since 2010, and a record number of teachers returning to the classroom, but we know there's more to do.

sentences.text: Lhamo Weston trains for her powerlifting competitions at a gym in Redditch A teenage powerlifter managed to win double golds at a world championship despite her endometriosis flaring up to leave her in excruciating pain just before the competition.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: Lhamo Weston, from Redditch, also landed second on the podium with a silver and a bronze medal, across three events in the World Sub-Junior & Junior Powerlifting Championships, in South Africa last month.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: Lhamo Weston placed second overall at the World Sub-Junior & Junior Powerlifting Championships Lhamo told the BBC she loves competing in the sport because of its inclusivity.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "I love how inclusive it is and how we're like a community," she said.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "Everyone knows each other and are really supportive of each other, and I just think it's an amazing sport that really brings people together." She stood on the podium in the Under 57kg category at the championship after getting two golds in squat and deadlift, and a bronze in the bench event.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "It felt incredible to be completely honest, I went into it with expectations of potentially reaching podium.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: Friends Amelia (left) and Beatrice (right) are living at home when they start university this September More new students are choosing to live at home for university this year than in the last nine years, new data shows.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Over 81,000 UK 18-year-olds said in their accepted university application that they intended to live at home this year, according to the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (Ucas) - just over one in three students in that category.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: In 2017, it was closer to one in five.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The figures vary across the UK - with 48% of applicants in Scotland intending to live at home, compared with 20% in Wales - but the trend is rising across the board.

sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem This July, during Britain's record-breaking hot summer, a curious row broke out on X over climate science.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Reform's deputy leader Richard Tice shared a Telegraph article headlined: "Heatwaves caused by fall in pollution." He said cleaner air, rather than carbon dioxide, was behind higher temperatures and claimed the public had been "gaslit".
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: He was wrong to suggest that carbon dioxide is not the primary driver of global warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But the science he was distorting is real - and much more interesting than his original claim.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The fossil fuels that we've been burning for more than a century produce two very different kinds of pollution.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: As is well known, carbon dioxide warms the Earth.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But less well-known is sulphur pollution, which forms vast numbers of tiny particles in the air and reflects sunlight back into space, partly counteracting the warming effect of carbon.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Thanks to clean-air policies around the world - like the US's Acid Rain Program in the early 1990s, that reduced gas pollution from power plants - sulphur emissions are falling sharply while carbon dioxide emissions remain near record highs.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Scientists increasingly believe the loss of that cooling effect is slightly speeding up global warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The past three years were the three warmest ever recorded, and the Met Office says 2027 is "very likely" to replace 2024 as the warmest year on record.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And away from social media, the argument over Tice's tweet raised an even more interesting - and worrying - question.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Is it possible that our planet is actually more sensitive to greenhouse gases than we imagined?
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And if so, might the climate be changing more rapidly than we feared?
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Global temperatures jump around naturally from year to year.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: El Niño, for example, a natural warming of the Pacific Ocean, can temporarily push them higher.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: So a run of record hot years does not necessarily mean the underlying rate of global warming has increased.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Reto Knutti and his team at ETH Zurich have tried to strip out the effects of El Niño and other natural fluctuations to reveal the underlying trend.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: "It's pretty clear that the rate of warming has accelerated," says Knutti, a professor of climate physics at the Swiss university and a former co-ordinating lead author for the IPCC - the UN-backed body that produces the world's most authoritative assessments of climate science.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: A separate study published this year reached a similar conclusion after accounting for several major natural influences.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And it seems aerosols are playing a role.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Burning coal and oil releases sulphur dioxide, which forms tiny particles known as sulphate aerosols.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: These particles are bright and reflect some sunlight before it can reach and warm the planet's surface.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Pollution from ships can create bright trails through clouds, visible from space You've probably heard the greenhouse analogy used to explain global warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Gases like carbon dioxide make it harder for heat to escape from the Earth, rather like the glass windows of a greenhouse.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Dorothea Bate, who died in 1951 aged 72, "transformed our understanding of prehistoric animals and ancient environments" through her research, Historic England said.

sentences.text: Bate was born in Carmarthen, Wales, in 1878 and developed a fascination with the natural world from an early age.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She moved with her family to rural Gloucestershire as a young woman and spent hours exploring the surrounding countryside and caves, collecting fossils.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She had little formal education, instead largely teaching herself, and in 1900 asked for work behind the scenes at the Natural History Museum in London.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: Her determination impressed museum staff, earning her a position as an assistant and beginning an association with the institution that would last more than 50 years.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She published her first scientific paper, A Short Account Of A Bone Cave In The Carboniferous Limestone Of The Wye Valley, in 1901.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: Bate went on to undertake expeditions across the Mediterranean, often travelling alone to remote caves in search of evidence of ancient life.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: In Cyprus, she discovered a previously unknown species of dwarf elephant and in 1909, while in the Balearics, she discovered the myotragus - an extinct goat-like antelope.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She achieved more than 80 published scientific papers, despite spending most of her career without a permanent paid position.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque
