sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: "She used this drive to make sense of ancient life through fragments of bone, bringing it to life once again," they said.

sentences.text: The air, amber-hued and treacle-thick, is smudged under a blanket of smog that has spilled across international borders – to Singapore, Manila, Kuala Lumpur.

sentences.text: Down on the ground, smoke steams from the soil.

sentences.text: And they're right." The 35-year-old volunteer firefighter has spent more than a month enveloped in this haze, breathing toxic millennia-old microparticles of carbon as he toils against a seemingly inextinguishable fire front.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Using hand tools, carts and portable fire pumps, he and thousands of other volunteer firefighters – many of them indigenous Dayak or Banjar people – are up against an inferno that has carbonised some 200,000 hectares of forest and farmland across Indonesian Borneo since early July.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Underground and out of sight, giant subterranean peat fires continue to smoulder, choking the air with poisonous fumes.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "Once a fire becomes uncontrolled, it harms many people.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Not just humans, but also animals and plants," Sujatmoko says.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "If underground fire spreads and can no longer be controlled, the losses are enormous." Fires have torched some 200,000 hectares across Indonesian Borneo since early July Indonesia is in the throes of a wildfire catastrophe.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Amid a so-called "Super El Niño" that has supercharged local drought conditions, thousands of active fire hotspots are spreading and multiplying across the country, fuelling a transnational haze crisis that is the region's worst in more than a decade.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: But what makes Borneo's fires particularly worrying is the fact that they are burning through one of the world's largest tropical peatland ecosystems.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: This 4.5-million-hectare swathe of forest and swamp, under normal conditions, serves as a valuable reservoir for ancient carbon.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: When these peatlands catch fire, they risk releasing millions of tonnes of carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and methane into the atmosphere – a "pulse" of greenhouse gas emissions that has earned them the sobriquet of "carbon bomb".
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "Peatlands are incredibly effective carbon stores because their waterlogged conditions slow decomposition, allowing carbon to accumulate underground for thousands of years," explains Dr Nisa Novita, a peatland researcher at Indonesian conservation NGO Yayasan Konservasi Alam Nusantara (YKAN).
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "But this also means they can become a 'carbon bomb' when they are drained or burned, because that carbon can be rapidly released into the atmosphere.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "Tropical peatlands in Indonesia are among the world's most effective natural carbon stores.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: The deeper the peat, the greater the carbon stock – and in Kalimantan, we have found peat deposits that can exceed 20 metres in depth." A peatland that deep has been known to harbour more than 6,000 tonnes of carbon – roughly equivalent to the annual CO₂ emissions of 4,800 cars – per hectare.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: And when it burns, says Dr Nisa, that fossilised carbon can be released into the atmosphere "very rapidly".
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "We're doing everything we can to help deal with this haze disaster because it's our duty," says firefighter Dwi Sujatmoko Thousands of people across South East Asia are now feeling the effects of those emissions in their eyes, chests and throats.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Across Indonesia as well as Brunei, Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines, air pollution indices have soared to "unhealthy" extremes - almost 75 times the World Health Organization's recommended level, in some cases – and hospital admissions have surged.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Between July and August, Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded over 50,000 cases of respiratory infections linked to land and forest fires.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: More than 12,000 of them were children under the age of five.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "Everybody who's living within that pollution cloud is breathing in the products of those smouldering peat fires," says Susan Page, a professor at the University of Leicester's school of geology and the environment, who's been researching peatlands in Asia for three decades.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "They're breathing in carbon monoxide, which is toxic, and they're breathing in the very finely divided particulate matter... [which] can pass through the alveoli in the lungs into the bloodstream and cause further problems elsewhere in the body, including issues with the heart.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "Living in this kind of pollution cloud is extremely unhealthy." Fighting peat fires requires saturating the ground so thoroughly that it becomes "like porridge" Nowhere are these health impacts being felt more acutely than at the coalface of the disaster: the fire front.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Here, volunteer firefighters have been risking their lives and lungs to extinguish burning peatlands which are notoriously difficult to put out.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Two volunteers  in Central Kalimantan have died in recent days, reportedly after their health deteriorated from putting out fires.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Cloaked in toxic haze that can burn years off a person's lifespan, volunteers have been digging ponds, canals and borewells through bone-dry peat in a desperate attempt to keep their hoses tapped.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Some have been driving pipes into the earth, making ad hoc irrigation systems to combat subterranean fires.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Others have been sleeping within a stone's throw of the frontline so they can battle the blazes through the night.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Experts say the crisis is rooted in decades of land-use change, dating back to the Suharto era, when vast areas of rainforest and peatland in Kalimantan were opened for logging, plantations and large-scale development projects.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Yet authorities have historically avoided blaming industrial actors for causing large-scale fires.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Instead, the same indigenous communities who are now engaged in firefighting operations across the island have often been accused of triggering the blazes, due to traditional farming methods that use controlled burns to clear away vegetation.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Tono, a representative of the Dayak Kanayatn people of West Kalimantan, told the BBC that Dayak communities are frequently used as scapegoats, despite carrying out land clearing with extensive planning, caution and adherence to multi-generational customs.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: Tono says these communities' traditional practices, known as uma bukit or "hill farming", are rooted in the idea of maintaining balance with nature.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "The worst thing here has been the smoke," says Fahrin Ramadhianto But the natural balance is fast unravelling in Kalimantan, the most deforested area in Indonesia.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: The region lost almost 160,000 hectares of forest area in 2025, more than one-third of the nationwide figure – much of it to make way for plantations and monocrop agriculture.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: It is these same industrial-scale development projects that have been largely responsible for draining the area's peat swamps, which renders them significantly more fire-prone, Prof Page says.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "Peatlands aren't really the ideal place to set up a plantation – but of course, once the more suitable mineral soils had been exhausted it became possible, by using large machinery, to drain the peatlands and create conditions which would be dry enough," she says.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "So not only have you got the deforestation, but peatland drainage of course has also greatly increased the fire risk." Page also points out that, whether on fire or not, a drained peatland emits carbon dioxide into the atmosphere "all of the time".
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "I think that's forgotten," she says.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "I think it's important to recognise that when we see the fires, they're like a dramatic example of what is actually going on the whole time in a drained peatland...

sentences.text: The fires are just the worst expression of [that]." Now, as these latest fires continue to spiral out of control, Sujatmoko and others face a concatenation of difficulties in the coming days, weeks and months – not least of which is a shortage of water.

sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: In the face of these persistent reignitions, ongoing drought conditions and toxic smog, fatigue is another concern.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "We're definitely tired," says Sujatmoko.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: "We get exhausted, we miss our families, our children, our wives.

sentences.text: But for now, all of us are putting those things aside.
sentences.article_title: The volunteers risking their lives to defuse Indonesia's wildfire 'carbon bombs'

sentences.text: We're doing everything we can to help deal with this haze disaster because it's our duty." "We also hope rain comes soon," he adds.

sentences.text: "We've spent months away from home...

sentences.text: Scientists may have found evidence of dark matter for the first time in an underground lab Scientists believe they may be one step closer to detecting dark matter for the first time, but the findings have not been verified by independent researchers.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Scientists from the University of Bristol were part of a two-year study to try and measure the invisible substance thought to make up over 85% of the universe.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Using a sensitive detector in an an underground laboratory in the US, the researchers saw an atom and mystery particle colliding.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Lead researcher physicist Dr Sam Eriksen said it could be "the first step in understanding dark matter as a particle", but further research could also reveal that the particle is not related to dark matter.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: "Following a huge amount of scientific effort, this is incredibly exciting," the University of Bristol senior research associate added.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Although scientists have long been certain of the existence of dark matter, because it is invisible as it reflects no light.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: While it is thought to make up the majority of mass in the universe, it has never been directly detected.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: It is managed by the US Department of Energy's Sanford Underground Research Facility in South Dakota - the deepest laboratory in the US at nearly a mile beneath the ground.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Scientists studied data from one of the world's most sensitive dark matter detectors To search for dark matter, LZ uses extremely sensitive light detectors to capture particle interactions.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: The study found one particle interaction which could potentially have been caused by a Weakly Interacting Massive Particle, (WIMP), which scientists believe make up dark matter.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: But there is currently low statistical evidence in it being a true breakthrough. 'I would be dead if I had not learnt about little-known law' How many times has Clare's Law been used in the West of England?

sentences.text: The normal threshold is five.

sentences.text: "With only one event, we don't want to get ahead of ourselves," said Professor Rick Gaitskell from Brown University.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: "We are not claiming to have seen dark matter.

sentences.text: Google will buy up to half the electricity produced by one of Finland's nuclear power plants as part of a record €13bn (£11bn; $15bn) investment in the country's AI infrastructure, the company announced.

sentences.text: The US tech giant said the package would fund three new data centres, expand an existing site and support energy projects to power growing demand for AI services.

sentences.text: Finland has emerged as an attractive location for data centres because of its cool climate, plentiful low-carbon electricity and relatively uncongested power grid.

sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: "Deepening our collaboration with Google will deliver lasting benefits for both parties." Google will build new data centres in Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala, while expanding its existing facility in Hamina, which it established after converting a former paper mill in 2009.

sentences.text: The world's largest LGBTQ+ dating app was sued in the High Court in 2024 over claims it misused people's personal information.

sentences.text: The class action suit was later served in the US, with the law firm leading the case saying it had signed up more than 11,000 claimants.

sentences.text: According to a US regulatory filing, Grindr will make two £13m payments to settle the claims.

sentences.text: The firm said the settlement includes no admission of liability.
sentences.article_title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status

sentences.text: Grindr stressed the claims relate to "historical data practices" before 2020 when it was owned by Chinese firm Kunlun.
sentences.article_title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status

sentences.text: The filing submitted to the US Securities and Exchange Commission , external by Grindr said a settlement had been reached on 2 September.
sentences.article_title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status

sentences.text: "While Grindr disputes the allegations, it recognizes and acknowledges the distress and loss of trust expressed by some of its UK users regarding that pre-2020 period," the company said in its filing.
sentences.article_title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status

sentences.text: The firm has agreed to pay £13m to the counterparties by 31 December and a further £13m by 31 March 2027.
sentences.article_title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status

sentences.text: The claims brought more than two years ago by law firm Austen Hayes alleged Grindr had shared sensitive data with third parties for commercial purposes, breaching UK privacy laws.
sentences.article_title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status

sentences.text: It said this included information about the ethnicity and sexual orientation of its users.
sentences.article_title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status

sentences.text: People on Grindr have the option to share their HIV status along with when they were last tested - a move it says aims to reduce stigma, facilitate conversations and help users make informed health choices.
sentences.article_title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status

sentences.text: Chaya Hanoomanjee, the lawyer who led the claim, said in April 2024 claimants had "experienced significant distress" over their sensitive and private information being shared without their consent.

sentences.article_title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status

sentences.article_title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status

sentences.text: Grindr defended the practice at the time as in line with industry standards – but it said it then stopped sharing HIV data with those companies.
sentences.article_title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status

sentences.text: It was fined £5.5m by Norway's data protection watchdog and, later in 2022, reprimanded by the UK Information Commissioner's Office for its data practices.

sentences.text: The White House has taken down a Tetris-style game on its website called "Build The Wall", days after The Tetris Company raised concerns over its use of the game's likeness.
sentences.article_title: White House pulls Tetris-style 'Build The Wall' game after copyright concern

sentences.text: The game, which saw players stack blocks to build a wall to "protect the border" is one of five arcade games which have appeared on the White House website.
sentences.article_title: White House pulls Tetris-style 'Build The Wall' game after copyright concern

sentences.text: On 4 September the official Tetris account on X posted , external the firm was "not involved in the creation" of the game and it took "copyright infringement very seriously".
sentences.article_title: White House pulls Tetris-style 'Build The Wall' game after copyright concern

sentences.text: The White House has not responded to requests for comment from the BBC or given an official reason for the takedown.
sentences.article_title: White House pulls Tetris-style 'Build The Wall' game after copyright concern

sentences.text: "At Tetris we believe in the power of connection and building people together, not dividing them," the firm said in its initial response to the game.
sentences.article_title: White House pulls Tetris-style 'Build The Wall' game after copyright concern

sentences.text: Four other arcade games still remain on the mini-game section of the White House website.
sentences.article_title: White House pulls Tetris-style 'Build The Wall' game after copyright concern

sentences.text: "Flappy Bill", a clone of the 2013 viral hit Flappy Bird sees players fly a bald eagle and dodging monuments from the National Mall.
sentences.article_title: White House pulls Tetris-style 'Build The Wall' game after copyright concern

sentences.text: OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has called for "extreme caution" over AI's runaway progress and warned more intervention may be needed to ensure "humans remain in control of the future".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: "I am concerned no one is prepared for the consequences of a continued rapid rise in machine intelligence," he wrote in a blog post entitled "An Alien Mind , external ".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: The post comes only a few days after the ChatGPT-maker released its latest model GPT-6 Astra, which it called its most powerful product ever.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: OpenAI and other AI firms like Anthropic shared reports of their AI agents acting autonomously and carrying out real-world cyber-attacks on other companies.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: In July, OpenAI called an incident in which its AI agents - AI systems which can operate alone after human instruction - hacked the tech platform Hugging Face "unprecedented".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: Meanwhile in September a report claimed months earlier AI agents from the firm had also hijacked a German website.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: "We are facing a transition to a world with incredibly intelligent machines, and we need to ensure that transition works out well for humanity," Pachocki wrote in the latest blog post.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: He said OpenAI would continue to "build defensive systems" and seek technical solutions to alignment - a term used to describe ensuring a machine's actions and goals perfectly match human intent and safety guardrails.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: Pachocki added one of the firm's main priorities moving forward would be to build an "automated AI researcher" to keep pace with AI progress while ensuring ways that human researchers could remain part of the process.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: "Instead of better AI guardrails, regulations, or assurance to keep people safe, they propose developing internal AI agents to research these problems," said Professor Gina Neff, head of the Minderoo Centre for Technology and Democracy at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: "If Jakub and others at OpenAI want relevant folks in the AI industry to act in concert with them to make things go well, one of the most important things they can do is share far more information about what they are seeing that is making them call for caution," he wrote on X , external .
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: Global regulations are struggling to keep up with the pace of AI development.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: The European Union's AI Act came into force on 2 August, which requires AI giants like OpenAI to prove their most powerful models cannot autonomously launch cyber-attacks or evade human control before they are allowed to be sold in Europe.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: But because the law's jurisdiction is confined to Europe, it cannot stop a rogue AI developed elsewhere from threatening the continent.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: In his blog post, Pachocki called for legally or internationally required minimum safety thresholds which could be enforced by a "network of third-party auditors" or "government agencies".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: AI labs would need to meet these thresholds, he said, before they were allowed to continue scaling or deploy advanced models.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: He added he hoped "voluntary slow downs" - a self-imposed pause by companies in AI development - would become commonplace until shared guardrails were established.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: In August OpenAI said it had slowed down training some of its most advanced AI models to improve security.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: Instagram creators say they have lost thousands of pounds after their accounts were suspended or taken down due to fake copyright claims.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Extorters have filed bogus claims to the Meta-owned social media platform, then asked for ransoms to withdraw them - knowing repeated claims can lead to account bans.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: One Instagram user, who has 1.5 million followers, told the BBC he paid a scammer $50 (£37) to get his account back, claiming Meta's appeal process would take weeks, which had previously cost him thousands in lost income.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: "We understand this can be frustrating for those impacted, and our systems are designed to protect people from this happening in the first place," a Meta spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: The Lost in Time History Instagram account posts historical pictures to its more than 1.5 million followers.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Its creator Olly, who did not share his last name, told the BBC he posts pictures in the public domain or where he has permission from the rights holder.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Yet he has received dozens of "obviously fake" copyright complaints so far in 2026.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Meta does not check the authenticity of complaints when they are made, so if someone is hit repeatedly, their account can be temporarily taken down.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Olly says he often gets struck for multiple posts at a time, all from the same email address.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: He then gets contacted by the person asking to go on to the private messaging app Telegram.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: "They'll demand a certain amount of money," he said - usually amounting to a few hundred dollars - to withdraw the claim.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: The BBC has seen messages from the claimants where they demand money or threaten future copyright strikes.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: This article contains content provided by Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: You may want to read Meta’s Instagram cookie policy , external and privacy policy , external before accepting.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: To view this content choose ‘accept and continue’ .
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Olly ultimately agreed to pay an extorter $50 in cryptocurrency to restore his account, which had been temporarily taken down by Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Law enforcement organisations tell extortion victims not to pay ransoms as it fuels the criminal ecosystem.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Olly said he paid as a "last resort" because it was quicker than going through Meta, which could take weeks.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: But he was hit by more copyright strikes immediately after he paid.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: "That's the worst part," he said.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: "Having to pay the person who's actively put you through all of that anguish only for it to happen straight away again." As a result of the number of times he has been hit by copyright claims, Olly's account was demonetised, meaning he could not earn money from Instagram for high-performing posts.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: "There's no investigation into abuse, or system detection [from Meta] that it could be abuse," he said.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Other Instagram users have shared similar experiences.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: "Meta was not helpful throughout the entire process, forcing you to pay for support to talk, even as they claim to be here for the creator," said Abin Tom Sebastian, who is behind the Morbid Kuriosity account.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Meta charges a £9.99 monthly fee to be Verified on Instagram, which gives users 24/7 access to support via a live chat.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: "I lost irrecoverable and crucial, brand contracts that unfortunately moved ahead with another creator, and no reassurance or support from Meta saying this will not happen again," Sebastian said.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Instagram says , external only copyright holders, or an authorised representative, can report copyright infringement, and it advises affected users to contacted rights holders directly.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: After the BBC contacted Meta with examples from Olly and other account holders, Meta said it had applied additional protections to their accounts, which it said would prevent similar issues happening in the future.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: It said it fought against deceptive behaviour to scam or defraud people and businesses.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: The BBC has spoken to three people who file copyright strikes against Instagram users, despite not being the copyright holders.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: All three appear to be based in India, or in countries nearby.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: They deny they are holding accounts to ransom - instead saying they file legitimate claims on behalf of copyright holders.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: But the BBC has seen messages from one where they ask for $900 (£668) to withdraw a strike.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: They claimed this was their payment for the service, and confirmed they kept all the money.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Two others denied they made any money at all.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: One said they are sent accounts to target and investigate the claim.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: "If I find that they are using someone else's content, I issue copyright strikes for the benefit of everyone," they said.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: The other said they are sent accounts or posts via an account holder or another representative.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Legitimate agencies do exist which are paid to file copyright strikes on behalf of clients.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: But Olly - who has dealt with these before when he has mistakenly posted copyrighted material - says they are usually easy to deal with, and "you can easily tell the difference".
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: "They're established companies with millions of followers, so it's very different," he said.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: These kinds of copyright scams are not new, with a version of the crime dating back to the early days of the internet, said Andres Guadamuz, reader in intellectual property law of the University of Sussex and an expert on digital copyright.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Previously, they were emails or letters sent to website owners claiming they owned the copyright to photos used online, and asking for money to avoid legal action.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: Similar strikes have been used against YouTube users too .
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: But the recent increase in this method may be because AI has made it easier to do this on a larger scale.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: "It's a numbers game," Guadamuz told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: "Pretty much anyone can now deploy [AI] that is going to automate all of this in some way," he said.
sentences.article_title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims

sentences.text: It is also harder for the platforms - with billions of users - to police the racket, and distinguish the real copyright claims from the fake ones.

sentences.text: "The system was almost built with the assumption that the person that was making a copyright strike claim was legitimate," he said.

sentences.text: The Mercator projection is the map widely used across the globe but inaccurately depicts the sizes of countries and continents The UN has just called for the predominant world map to be replaced with one that more accurately reflects the true size of continents such as Africa.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Equal Earth map aims to represent landmasses' area more fairly The Equal Earth map aims to address this problem with the Mercator projection.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The straight lines on the Peters map also do not represent true constant compass bearings and so are useless for navigation.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: And depending on where you are in the world, which continent is placed in the centre of a map can vary.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: While these alternate maps offer a different perspective on the world to the one we may be familiar with, they don't solve the issue of prominence, but rather simply change the focus of a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN flag is centred on the North Pole so no one continent is the primary focus One way of resolving the issue of which landmass is at the centre of a map - and therefore the most prominent - is putting none of them at the centre.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This is what the map in the UN logo does: the world is centred around the North Pole, with the continents radiating outward from it.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It's known as an "Azimuthal equidistant projection", placing world regions on a circular map around a focal point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The further away from that point on the globe, the bigger the circle.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On this type of map, all points are at the correct "azimuth" - or horizontal direction - from the centre point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But to fit the entire surface of a sphere onto a circle, the map becomes more distorted the further away from the centre it gets.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On the UN map, for instance, areas near the South Pole appear squished and stretched as what would be a ring of the same circumference as one around the North Pole becomes much larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Manasse Lomachar would like the discovery of gold to improve life in his village A goat herder from a remote area of western Kenya has told the BBC his discovery of a golden nugget has sparked a gold rush, overwhelming his small village over the last few weeks.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: When people found out that 33-year-old Manasse Lomachar had sold his three grams of gold for 36,000 Kenyan shillings ($280; £205) several weeks ago, he believes this led to the arrival of thousands of prospectors in Cheporor.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: And it is true that what last month was just bushland and rough grazing ground near the village is now scarred by pits, mounds of earth and makeshift mining camps.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: It is not clear if was Lomachar's lucky find or other recent discoveries that sparked the excitement.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: But local authorities estimate that about 10,000 people arrived at the height of the rush.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Even a small amount of the precious metal can transform the futures of these men and women - from Kenya and neighbouring Uganda - many of whose precarious lives rest on an unreliable farming income.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Large numbers of people have been searching through the earth and rocks for any sign of the precious metal People do sometimes pan for gold in these parts - but rarely find anything significant.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Lomachar's says his discovery came about purely by chance.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: While he was searching for a missing goat he encountered a group of women panning along a riverbed.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: "I joined them, and that's how [the village] realised there was gold in this area," he says.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Farmer and herder Patrick Lokolia, from neighbouring Napawoi village, joined the gold rush hoping to earn some extra money to support his family.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: "I have children in school, and paying school fees has been a big problem for me," he tells the BBC wearing an old Chelsea football top and standing amid the mining activity.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Eighteen-year-old Abigael Chelengat says she had never mined before coming to Cheporor from a nearby district, but arrived hoping to find enough gold to pay her school fees and help keep her younger siblings in school.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Abigael Chelengat hopes a gold find will help her pay for her education Behind her hundreds of people work side by side, hacking into the rocky ground with hoes and shovels.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Others carry the earth to a nearby seasonal river, where mostly women crouch in the murky water, washing and sifting mud and sand hoping to detect a tiny trace of the element.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Some of the more experienced miners are deep in holes excavating the earth and drilling at rocks with the same goal.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Hope is kept alive by stories of those for whom the effort has paid off - like Lomachar.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Samuel Kiarie, the deputy commissioner of West Pokot county, says he thinks the rush began after two notable discoveries.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: "Young men found what appeared to be a substantial amount of gold.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: The following day, women made another significant find in the same area," he tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Kiarie explains that women have been finding small quantities of alluvial gold along the same seasonal riverbed for years, typically earning $8-$23 a week.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Many of those who have come are not experienced miners But the uncovering of larger quantities at the beginning of August is what caught the attention of many people.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Kiarie reckons as rumours spread, the number and size of the discoveries were exaggerated - drawing in ever larger groups of people with little or no mining experience who hoped to replicate the reported early successes.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Since the initial rush, the number of prospectors has gone down to around 2,500 as some have given up the search.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: While there is little doubt that some gold has been found in the area, questions remain about the size of the deposit in the earth and its commercial potential.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: "I can confirm that small-scale gold traders told us they received an average of about 100 people every day," the deputy commissioner says - though whether the finds were actually gold is not known.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Individual discoveries reportedly range from amounts worth a few hundred Kenyan shillings to one find valued at approximately 78,000 shillings ($600).
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: West Pokot county borders Uganda, and communities on both sides have long-standing social and family ties.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Mugisha Godfrey, an artisanal miner from Busia in eastern Uganda, travelled to Cheporor after hearing about the discovery from a friend.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: He immediately set out for the village spending about 100,000 Ugandan shillings ($27) to get there.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: However, the living conditions in Cheporor are not favourable, he says.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: "We sleep under the trees, and when morning comes, we continue working.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Sometimes we work both day and night," Godfrey tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: So far, he has found nothing.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: But he is not discouraged.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: "We can't return unless we find something.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Only when we have found what we need can we go back home," he says.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: The authorities want to make sure that children leave the site come September when the school term starts For others, the gold rush has created opportunities without requiring them to dig.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: More than 200 businesses have emerged around the site, according to local officials, selling food, water and other essentials to the village's new population.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Irene Ameja travelled from neighbouring Baringo county to cater to the crowds.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: She sells bottled water, soft drinks, bread, milk and other foodstuffs.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: "I am hoping that when I leave, I will have made enough money to continue with my business and expand it," she says.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: But the rapid growth of the settlement has also exposed the area's lack of basic services.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: "This is a forest and we are in the middle of the mountains," she says.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Public health officials have been deployed to monitor conditions and help prevent disease outbreaks.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: The authorities say they have also increased security patrols amid concerns over sexual violence and the vulnerability of women and girls at the site.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: As the search continues miners are digging ever-deeper holes Officials are also worried that children could be drawn into mining activities as schools prepare to reopen in September.

sentences.text: Measures are being put in place to discourage young people from remaining at the site once the new school term begins.

sentences.text: Those still searching are increasingly turning to deeper excavation.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Until then, the size and commercial viability of any mining remain uncertain.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: For Lomachar, the answer is not to stop the mining, but to make it more organised.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Joy-Lance Mickels is set to be the first player from Rwanda to feature in the Champions League proper Joy-Lance Mickels has been a Manchester United fan since childhood, and on Thursday the Rwanda international will fulfil a lifelong dream.

sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.text: "Reaching the Champions League is an historic achievement for Sabah and starting the league phase at Old Trafford makes it even more exciting," Mickels said.
sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.text: "At the same time, we're not going there only to enjoy the atmosphere.
sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.text: His first spell with Sabah came between 2021 and 2023, and he returned to the Bank Respublika Arena two years ago.
sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.text: "My career has not always followed a straight or easy path," he explained.
sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.text: "I have played at different levels and in several countries.
sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.text: "I'm very proud of my Rwandan roots," he said.
sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd

sentences.text: "Representing Rwanda whilst playing the Champions League is very, very special.
sentences.article_title: The Rwandan eyeing Champions League history against Man Utd
